events.region: Fisher; Nolan; Sterling; Coke; Runnels; Irion; Tom Green; Concho; Crockett; Schleicher; Sutton; Haskell; Throckmorton; Jones; Shackelford; Taylor; Callahan; Coleman; Brown; McCulloch; San Saba; Menard; Kimble; Mason
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The combination of an upper level storm system, increasing
moisture and temperatures in the 30s may produce a few hours of
light snow mainly west of a Sterling City to Throckmorton line
Tuesday morning. Expect little to no accumulation of snowfall.
However, there is a low chance of local accumulations around 1/2
of an inch which may cause a few slick spots on roads. The rest of
west central Texas will only see rain showers Tuesday morning.
Keep up with the latest weather information this week.

Also, expect colder temperatures across the area. A widespread
freeze is expected Wednesday morning with lows in the mid to upper
20s, possibly a few degrees colder in low lying areas and river
valleys. Highs will only be in the 40s Tuesday. Please prepare
for the colder weather.

events.region: Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico AND USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N; Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM; Coastal Waters from Cabo San Juan to the waters between Anegada Island and Virgin Gorda and North 10 NM; Coastal Waters east of Puerto Rico, around Vieques, and around and just north of Culebra and Saint John
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...
Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...
Coastal Waters from Cabo San Juan to the waters between Anegada
Island and Virgin Gorda and North 10 NM...
Coastal waters east of Puerto Rico, around Vieques, and around and
just north of Culebra and Saint John...

* At 303 AM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These strong
thunderstorms were located over open waters, eastern Atlantic
waters and coastal waters east of Puerto Rico, around Vieques, and
around and just north of Culebra and Saint John zones, moving east
at 5 knots.

rainfall continues.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

events.region: Foothills of the Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, visibility of one quarter mile
or less in dense fog and freezing fog. For the Wind Advisory for
the base and slopes of the northern Blue Mountains, southeast winds
25 to 35 mph with gusts of 40 to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...Foothills of the Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon.

* WHEN...For the Dense Fog Advisory, until 11 AM PST Monday. For the
Wind Advisory, from 7 PM Monday to 4 AM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Low
visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will be lighter away from the base of
the Blue Mountains.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides
and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during
periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas
along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.3 and 9.8 feet
MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal
Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm
surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in
King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101
Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
